# What visitors see, day by day

*Made by `node tools/season_calendar.mjs` from the pages themselves. Do not edit by hand: run the command again after changing the season dates, a `data-until`, a release row, or any wording in the first screen (`--check` says whether this page is out of date).*

The site changes with the calendar: seasons, the line under the headline, which buttons show, the open-now badges, the pizza chip, the schedule box, the countdown, the “New” tags, the footer year. This page lists what a visitor sees on every day from **Oct 3, 2026** to **Dec 31, 2027**, so the owner can look at a date and know.

**How it was looked at.** Each day, the home page and the five other pages were opened in English, at phone width (390 px), with the page clock set to **noon in New York** on that day (the farm’s day, whatever time zone the visitor is in). A sample was taken every 7 days and next to every date written in the page files and every season change; every gap between two different looks was halved until the exact day was found. Days with the same look on all six pages are one row below.

**What it does not show.** Hours of the day (the badges say “Open now” only Friday to Sunday daytime; at 5:00 PM on a release Tuesday the pizza chip says “open now” for six hours), the owner’s own settings in `js/content.js` (`notice`, `closures`, `week`: they are empty today, so none of them shows), other languages, and the top bar line on phones (it is hidden below 761 px).

Contents: 1. Date ranges · 2. Every change, in date order · 3. Things that look wrong on some days · 4. Tags that never switch off

## 2. Every change, in date order

The first day a different page is shown, what switched, why, and which setting or file controls it. “Pages” says where the change is seen.

| First day | What switches | Why | Controlled by |

## 3. Things that look wrong on some days

Found by checking every day’s pages against a few plain rules (listed in `RULES` in `tools/season_calendar.mjs`). Nothing here is decided for the owner: each item says what a visitor sees and what could be done. An item can be on purpose (for example, the farm may take reservations between seasons).

### A date that has already passed is written on the page as if it were still to come

*Suggestion: Give the line a data-until (the last day it is true) so it hides itself, or write it without a date (“every weekend in fall”).*

| Days | Where | What a visitor sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Oct 4, 2026 | Home page | “Oct 2 & 3” in “Open now: pizza reservations for Oct 2 & 3. We haven’t opened Sunday,…” |
| Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2027 | Home page | “Fall 2026” in “Fall 2026 prices for a farm visit, plus the snacks and drinks at the…” |
| Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2027 | Pumpkin patch page | “Fall 2026” in “Fall 2026 prices” |
| Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2027 | Home page | “Fall 2026” in “Fall 2026 reservations” |

### The farm’s “Reserve” buttons show while no season is in progress

*Suggestion: Add data-in-season to those buttons (they then hide between seasons and “Tell me when” shows instead), or keep them if the farm takes reservations all year. Owner decision.*

| Days | Where | What a visitor sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nov 9 – Nov 17, 2026; Aug 12 – Sep 12, 2027; Nov 9 – Nov 17, 2027 | Home page | shown: “Reserve a fall visit” · “Reserve the farm” · “Reserve your visit” (no season in progress) |
| Nov 18 – Nov 26, 2026; Dec 9, 2026 – Feb 9, 2027; Nov 18 – Nov 25, 2027; Dec 9 – Dec 31, 2027 | Home page | shown: “Reserve your visit” (no season in progress) |
| Nov 27 – Dec 8, 2026; Nov 26 – Dec 8, 2027 | Home page | shown: “Reserve your visit” (only winter, the Christmas trees, is in progress) |
| Feb 10 – Apr 14, 2027; Jun 8 – Jun 11, 2027 | Home page | shown: “Reserve a strawberry visit” · “Reserve the farm” · “Reserve your visit” (no season in progress) |
| Jun 12 – Jun 14, 2027; Jul 11 – Aug 11, 2027 | Home page | shown: “Reserve a summer visit” · “Reserve the farm” · “Reserve your visit” (no season in progress) |

### The page wears a season’s look while no season is in progress (the look follows the nearest season, not the date)

*Suggestion: Decide whether between seasons the page should keep the nearest season’s look (today) or a neutral look; the farm Reserve buttons could carry data-in-season so they hide when no season is open.*

| Days | Where | What a visitor sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nov 9 – Nov 17, 2026; Aug 12 – Sep 12, 2027; Nov 9 – Nov 17, 2027 | Home page | dressed as Fall (the nearest season) with no season in progress |
| Nov 18 – Nov 26, 2026; Dec 9, 2026 – Feb 9, 2027; Nov 18 – Nov 25, 2027; Dec 9 – Dec 31, 2027 | Home page | dressed as Winter (the nearest season) with no season in progress |
| Feb 10 – Apr 14, 2027; Jun 8 – Jun 11, 2027 | Home page | dressed as Spring (the nearest season) with no season in progress |
| Jun 12 – Jun 14, 2027; Jul 11 – Aug 11, 2027 | Home page | dressed as Summer (the nearest season) with no season in progress |

**Checked on every day and found nothing:** a link points to something that is not on the page that day; the first screen has no headline, or no line under it; an empty heading or an empty box is showing; a line says “It’s … season!”, or a “now” tag sits on a season, that is not in progress; two lines say different things; a script error on some days.

## 4. Tags that never switch off

On the home page these small labels are shown on every day in the range (nothing turns them off): “Now booking”, “Prices coming soon”, “TRADITIONAL FALL SCHOOL TOURS — NOW BOOKING”. Nothing in the page ties them to a date: when one stops being true it has to be edited by hand.
